observation.visible_scene: Two adults stand in profile facing each other in front of a black curtain: on the left a blonde woman in a red turtleneck sweater, smiling; on the right a bald, white-bearded man in a green-and-white plaid shirt. Several iridescent soap bubbles hang and drift in the open space between them.
visible_changes: The man's head, level at the start (gazing toward the woman), progressively tilts upward through the clip so that by the end he looks up at the bubbles and his mouth opens.
The woman stays essentially stationary in her smiling profile pose, with only minor body shifts.

The bubbles translate slowly and continuously in the air between the two people; their positions relative to each other and to the people change gradually from frame to frame (e.g. the upper bubble descends/drifts and the mid-level bubble shifts downward and toward the man).
One bubble near the top of the frame changes shape, going from a round form to an irregular, elongated/deformed blob and back toward roundness, while remaining a single object rather than splitting.
The black-curtain background and the framing of the two people do not change, indicating no camera movement during the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the bubbles were generated or blown, and what triggered the man's upward gaze.
Whether the deforming bubble pops, merges, or survives after the last frame.
What happens between the two people before the clip begins or after it ends.
uncertain_details: Exact per-bubble trajectories are hard to follow because reflections and overlapping colors make it ambiguous which bubble is which across frames.
Whether the top bubble's irregular shape is a deformation of the same bubble or a brief occlusion/merge with another bubble.
Precise timing of the man's head tilt relative to a specific bubble is gradual and not tied to a single frame.
